sub: Named after al-wāqiʿah, “the Occurrence”, in ayah 1
theme: The Hereafter made certain. On the Day people split into three groups, creation proves Allah can raise the dead, the Quran is true, and at death each group meets its end.
story: Revealed in Makkah, early on. Before ʿUmar became Muslim, his sister reportedly quoted ayah 79 to him (“only the purified touch it”), so the surah was already known. The Prophet ﷺ reportedly said that Hūd, al-Wāqiʿah and a few others had turned his hair grey.

The Makkan disbelievers found the resurrection unbelievable. Once they and their forefathers were dust and bones, how could they be raised, judged, and sent to Paradise or Hell? They also claimed the Quran was magic, or brought by devils.

The surah answers step by step. The Day will come and sort everyone into three groups. Their own creation, crops, water and fire prove Allah can raise them. The Quran is noble and protected. And at death, each person meets his group’s end.

sections.title: The Occurrence strikes, the earth crumbles, and people split into three groups
sections.meaning: When the Occurrence comes, no one can deny it. It lowers some and raises others. The earth is shaken, the mountains crumble to dust, and people become three groups: those on the right, those on the left, and the foremost, brought nearest to Allah in gardens of delight.
points: When the Occurrence occurs, no one can deny it
It brings some down and raises others up
The earth shaken, the mountains crushed into scattered dust
Three kinds: those on the right, those on the left
And the foremost, brought near, in gardens of delight
sections.matters: It sets out the plan of the whole surah. The three groups named here are described one by one in 10–56, then return at the moment of death in 88–94. It also warns that the Day overturns worldly rank.
sections.story: No specific incident. It answers the Makkan disbelievers, who thought the resurrection could never really happen.
explained: Al-wāqiʿah, the Occurrence, is a name for the Day of Resurrection, because it will surely happen. When it comes, no one can call it false or stop it. It is khāfiḍah rāfiʿah: it drops some to the Fire, even if they were mighty, and lifts others to Paradise, even if they were weak.

The earth is shaken violently and the mountains are ground into scattered dust. People then become three groups. Those on the right: how great their state! Those on the left: how terrible! And as-sābiqūn, who raced ahead to good in this life, race ahead into Paradise, brought nearest to Allah.
teaches: The Day is certain; denying it changes nothing.
Worldly rank means nothing then: the Day lowers and raises.
Everyone ends up in one of three groups, so choose yours now.
Race to good deeds here to be foremost there.
sections.hook: Ayat 1–2 use w-q-ʿ three times (waqaʿat, al-wāqiʿah, waqʿatihā). Ayat 8–10 name the groups right, left, foremost, but the descriptions run foremost (10), right (27), left (41).

sections.title: The foremost’s reward: jewelled thrones, ageless servants, pure drink, only peace
sections.meaning: The foremost are a large group of the earlier people and a few of the later. They recline on jewelled thrones, facing each other. Ageless youths bring drink that causes no headache or drunkenness, with any fruit and meat they want, and companions like hidden pearls. They hear no idle talk, only “peace”.
points: A large group of the earlier people, a few of the later
On woven thrones, reclining, facing each other
Ageless youths bring cups from a spring: no headache, no drunkenness
Any fruit they choose, any bird meat they desire
Ḥūr ʿīn like hidden pearls, a reward for their deeds
No idle or sinful talk, only “Peace, peace”
sections.matters: It shows the highest rank in Paradise, and ayah 24 says how it is reached: all of it is “a reward for what they used to do”. Every pleasure is complete, with none of this world’s flaws.
sections.story: No specific incident. Reportedly, “a few of the later people” (14) weighed on the Companions, and ayat 39–40 later answered them.
explained: Thullah means a large crowd. Either the nations before the Prophet ﷺ, with a few from his ummah, or the early generations of this ummah, with fewer from its later ones. They sit on thrones woven with gold and jewels, reclining and facing one another, no one behind another’s back.

Youths who never age go round with cups, jugs and a glass from a flowing spring. It gives no headache and doesn’t take away the mind. Fruit and bird meat come as they wish, with wide-eyed companions pure as hidden pearls. No foul or sinful word is heard, only greetings of peace.
teaches: The highest rank goes to those who rush to good.
Paradise’s pleasures have none of this world’s harms.
Reward matches deeds: “a reward for what they used to do.”
Clean, kind speech is the speech of Paradise.
sections.hook: Paired lines: thullah then qalīl (13–14), mimmā yatakhayyarūn then mimmā yashtahūn (20–21). The foremost open with a doubled word, as-sābiqūn as-sābiqūn (10), and close with one, salāman salāmā (26).

sections.title: The reward of those on the right: thornless trees, shade, fruit, spouses
sections.meaning: Then those on the right. They live among thornless lote trees and layered banana trees, in endless shade, by flowing water, with fruit never out of season or reach, on raised couches. Their wives are made anew: young, loving, of equal age. They are many from the earlier people and many from the later.
points: Those on the right: what a state they are in!
Thornless lote trees, layered banana trees, extended shade
Flowing water, endless fruit, raised couches
Wives created anew: virgins, loving, equal in age
A large group of the earlier people and a large group of the later
sections.matters: It describes the rank of the righteous believers: a step below the foremost, yet full of blessing. Its last pair (39–40) gives the later generations a large share too, unlike the foremost’s “few” in ayah 14.
sections.story: Reportedly, Muslims admired the lote trees of Wajj, a fertile valley near Ṭāʾif, and wished for the like, and ayah 28 came. And when ayah 14 worried the Companions, 39–40 reportedly came in reply.
explained: The lote tree of this world is thorny with little fruit. Paradise’s has no thorns and is heavy with fruit. Ṭalḥ is the banana tree, its fruit stacked from bottom to top, or a large shade tree. The shade stretches on, water flows constantly, and fruit is never out of season or out of reach.

The couches are raised high. Their wives are created anew: either the ḥūr, made without birth, or the women of this world made young again. They are virgins, ʿurub (loving to their husbands) and atrāb (all of one age). This group is large from the earlier people and large from the later.
teaches: Even the rank below the foremost is beyond imagination.
Paradise removes every flaw of this world’s blessings: thorns, seasons, limits.
No one enters Paradise old; all are made young.
Aim to be foremost, and never lose hope of the right.
sections.hook: Ayah 27 repeats the question of ayah 8, but maymanah becomes yamīn. Makhḍūd, manḍūd, mamdūd (28–30) rhyme. Thullah comes twice in 39–40, where 13–14 had thullah then qalīl.

sections.title: Those on the left: smoke, zaqqūm and boiling water, for denying resurrection
sections.meaning: Those on the left are in scorching wind and boiling water, under a shade of black smoke that gives no relief. They lived in luxury, kept up the great sin, and mocked being raised from dust. Say: every generation will be gathered. Then they will eat zaqqūm and drink like thirsty camels.
points: Scorching wind, boiling water, black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant
They lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin
They said: once dust and bones, raised again, and our fathers?
Say: earlier and later will all be gathered on a known Day
Eating zaqqūm, bellies full, drinking boiling water like thirsty camels
That is their welcome on the Day of Recompense
sections.matters: It explains what led them there: luxury that distracted them, sin without repentance, and denial of the resurrection. Their own question (47–48) is answered on the spot (49–50), and it sets up the proofs that follow.
sections.story: No specific incident. Ayat 47–48 quote the Makkan disbelievers’ own objection to being raised after becoming dust and bones.
explained: Samūm is a scorching wind of the Fire, ḥamīm boiling water, yaḥmūm thick black smoke whose shade is neither cool nor pleasant. Why? They were mutrafīn, living in comfort that distracted them from obedience, and persisted in al-ḥinth al-ʿaẓīm, shirk or great sin, without repenting. They mocked: raised from dust, even our forefathers?

Say: the earlier and later generations will all be gathered on a known Day. Then you who strayed and denied will eat from the zaqqūm tree until your bellies are full, then drink boiling water like al-hīm, camels whose thirst never ends. That is their nuzul, their “welcome meal”, on the Day of Recompense.
teaches: Comfort becomes dangerous when it distracts from obedience.
Persisting in sin without repentance is a crime of its own.
Mocking the resurrection doesn’t delay it.
What you send ahead here is the welcome you receive there.
sections.hook: Kānū opens 45, 46 and 47, the three causes. The shade is mamdūd for the right (30) but min yaḥmūm here (43). Fa-shāribūn comes back to back (54, 55).

sections.title: We created you and decreed death; the first creation proves the second
sections.meaning: Allah created you, so why not believe you will be raised? Do you create the fluid you emit, or does He? He has decreed death for all, and nothing stops Him replacing you or remaking you in forms you do not know. You know the first creation, so why not reflect?
points: We created you, so why do you not believe?
The fluid you emit: do you create it, or do We?
We decreed death, and can replace you or remake you
You know the first creation, so why not take heed?
sections.matters: The proofs begin. The surah answers the question of 47–48 with what everyone already knows: they did not make themselves, and the One who made them once can make them again.
sections.story: No specific incident. It answers the denial of the resurrection quoted in 47–48.
explained: We brought you into being from nothing, so why deny We can do it again? Look at the fluid you emit. Do you make it settle in the womb and grow, stage by stage, into a person, or does Allah?

We decreed death among you, and no one outruns Us. We could replace you with others like you, or remake you in forms you do not know. You already know how you were made the first time, so remember: whoever began creation can easily bring it back.
teaches: Your own creation is the clearest proof of resurrection.
People play a small part; Allah creates.
Death is decreed for everyone, and no one outruns Allah.
The One who began creation can surely repeat it.
sections.hook: Naḥnu opens 57 and 60. Fa-lawlā ends 57 (tuṣaddiqūn) and 62 (tadhakkarūn). Afa-raʾaytum in 58 is the first of four such questions.

sections.title: Who grows crops, sends rain and makes fire? So glorify your Lord
sections.meaning: Three more questions. The seed you sow: do you make it grow? He could turn it to chaff, leaving you lamenting. The water you drink: did you bring it from the clouds? He could make it salty. The fire you light: did you grow its tree? So glorify your Lord, the Most Great.
points: The seed you plant: do you grow it, or do We?
It could turn to chaff: “We are ruined; we are deprived!”
The water you drink: He could make it salty, so be grateful
The fire you kindle: who produced its tree?
A reminder and a benefit for travellers, so glorify your Lord
sections.matters: Food, water and fire are what daily life depends on. Each question shows that people do the small part and Allah does the rest. The fitting response is gratitude and tasbīḥ, which is exactly where the section ends.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the proofs of Allah’s oneness and His power to raise the dead.
explained: You plough and drop the seed, but who makes it sprout and ripen? If Allah willed, it would become dry chaff, leaving you stunned and full of regret: “We have lost what we spent. No, we are deprived.” The water you drink: did you bring it down from the clouds? He could make it too salty to drink.

The fire you strike from green wood: did you grow the tree? Allah made it a reminder of Hellfire and a provision for al-muqwīn, travellers in empty land, or anyone who uses it. So declare the perfection of your Lord’s name, the Most Great.
teaches: You sow, but only Allah makes it grow.
Any blessing could be spoiled; thank Allah that it wasn’t.
Fresh water is a mercy, and its answer is shukr.
The fire of this world is a reminder of the Fire.
sections.hook: Afa-raʾaytum returns at 63, 68 and 71. Each “you, or We?” ends in a title: az-zāriʿūn (64), al-munzilūn (69), al-munshiʾūn (72). Fa-sabbiḥ bismi rabbika al-ʿaẓīm (74) is also the surah’s last ayah.

sections.title: By the setting stars: a noble, protected Quran, yet you deny it
sections.meaning: Allah swears by the places where the stars set, a mighty oath if you knew. This is a noble Quran, in a protected Book that only the purified touch, sent down by the Lord of the worlds. Yet you treat it lightly, and make denial your thanks for your provision.
points: I swear by the settings of the stars, a mighty oath
A noble Quran, in a well-protected Book
Only the purified touch it; sent down from the Lord of the worlds
You take this lightly and repay your provision with denial
sections.matters: After proofs from creation, the surah turns to the Quran itself, the source of everything it has said. It answers the claim that it was magic or brought by devils: it is protected at its source, and only the pure angels reach it.
sections.story: Reportedly, after rain fell, some people said “such-and-such star brought us rain”, and 75–82 came in reply. The disbelievers also claimed devils brought the Quran; this passage denies it.
explained: Fa-lā uqsimu: No! It is not as you claim. I swear by the places where the stars set; if you knew, you would see how great this oath is. The Quran is karīm: noble and full of good. It is written in a kitāb maknūn, a guarded Book, the Preserved Tablet, beyond the devils’ reach.

Only al-muṭahharūn touch it: the angels, purified of sin. Many also take from it that the muṣḥaf is touched only in a state of purity. It is sent down from the Lord of the worlds. So do you treat this speech lightly, and make your thanks for rain nothing but denial?
teaches: The Quran is guarded at its source; devils cannot touch or change it.
Honour the muṣḥaf: touch it in a state of purity.
Never take the Quran lightly or hide it out of fear of people.
Rain comes from Allah’s favour, not from the stars.
sections.hook: Fa-lā uqsimu (75) opens the third ruku. Maknūn moves from the pearls (23) to the Book (78). Karīm, denied to the smoke’s shade (44), now describes the Quran (77).

sections.title: No one can return a dying soul; three groups meet their ends
sections.meaning: When the soul reaches the throat, you watch helplessly, and Allah is nearer than you. If there is no reckoning, bring it back! Then the three groups return: the brought-near get rest and a garden, those on the right hear “peace”, the deniers get boiling water and Hellfire. This is certain, so glorify your Lord.
points: The soul at the throat; you watch, but We are nearer
If you won’t be judged, bring it back, if you are truthful
The brought-near: rest, provision and a garden of delight
Those on the right: “Peace to you”
The deniers astray: boiling water and burning in Hellfire
This is certain truth, so glorify your Lord, the Most Great
sections.matters: The surah ends where every person ends: at death. No one can hold back a departing soul, so no one can escape the reckoning. The three groups of the Day return, now at the moment of death, when each person already learns his end.
sections.story: No specific incident. It closes the reply to those who denied they would be raised and judged.
explained: Fa-lawlā: then why not? When a dying man’s soul reaches his throat, his family stands watching, powerless. Allah is nearer to him, by His knowledge and His angels, but they cannot see. If they will truly never be raised and repaid, let them return the soul to its body. They cannot.

The brought-near get rawḥ (rest, mercy) and rayḥān (provision, fragrance) and a garden of delight. The one on the right is greeted: “Peace to you, you are of the people of the right.” The denier’s welcome is boiling water and burning in Hellfire. Ḥaqq al-yaqīn: this is certain truth.
teaches: Death shows how little control we really have.
Allah is nearer to the dying than those around him.
Each person’s end starts to show at death.
Say subḥāna rabbiya al-ʿaẓīm in rukūʿ, as this ayah taught.
sections.hook: Ammā in kāna opens 88, 90 and 92 in the order of 10–56: brought near, right, deniers. Aḍ-ḍāllūn al-mukadhdhibūn (51) returns reversed in 92. Ayah 96 repeats 74 exactly.

groups.text: When the Occurrence comes, no one can deny it. It lowers some people and raises others.
The earth is shaken violently, and the mountains are crushed into scattered dust.
People become three kinds: those on the right, how great their state, and those on the left, how terrible.
And the foremost, who raced to good, are foremost: brought near to Allah in gardens of delight.
They are a large group from the earlier people and a few from the later.
They recline on thrones woven with gold and jewels, facing one another.
Ageless youths serve them cups from a flowing spring that brings no headache and no drunkenness.
Any fruit they choose and any bird meat they desire.
Wide-eyed companions like hidden pearls, all a reward for what they used to do.
They hear no idle or sinful talk there, only greetings of peace.
Those on the right are among thornless lote trees and layered banana trees, in shade that never ends.
Flowing water, plentiful fruit never cut off or kept from them, and raised couches.
Their wives are created anew: virgins, loving to their husbands, all of one age, for those on the right.
They are a large group from the earlier people and a large group from the later.
Those on the left are in scorching wind and boiling water, under black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant.
They lived in luxury, persisted in the great sin, and mocked being raised from dust and bones.
Say: the earlier and later generations will all be gathered on a known Day.
You who strayed and denied will eat from the zaqqūm tree and fill your bellies with it.
Then drink boiling water like thirsty camels. That is their welcome on the Day of Recompense.
Allah created you, so why not believe? Do you create the fluid you emit, or does He?
He decreed death and can replace or remake you. You know the first creation, so why not reflect?
Do you grow what you sow? Allah could turn it to chaff, and you would lament your loss.
Did you send down the water you drink? He could make it salty, so why not be grateful?
Did you grow the tree that gives your fire? It is a reminder and a provision, so glorify your Lord.
Allah swears by the places where the stars set, a mighty oath if you only knew.
This is a noble Quran in a guarded Book, touched only by the purified, sent down by the Lord of the worlds.
Yet you treat this speech lightly and make denial your thanks for your provision.
When the soul reaches the throat, you watch helplessly, while Allah is nearer to the dying than you.
If you won’t be raised and judged, then bring the soul back, if you are truthful.
If he was one of those brought near: rest, provision and a garden of delight.
If he was of those on the right, he is greeted: “Peace to you.”
If he was a denier gone astray: a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hellfire.
This is the certain truth, so glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.

1.explain: Idhā waqaʿati al-wāqiʿah: when the Occurrence occurs. Al-wāqiʿah is a name for the Day of Resurrection, called that because it will certainly happen.

2.explain: Laysa li-waqʿatihā kādhibah: when it comes, no one can deny it, and nothing can stop or reverse it. The news of it is not false.

3.explain: Khāfiḍah rāfiʿah: it lowers some to the Fire, even if they were mighty in this world, and raises others to Paradise, even if they were weak. Or: its sound reaches both near and far.

4.explain: Rujjat: the earth is shaken violently, across its surface and through its depths, like a sieve shaken with everything in it.

5.explain: Bussat: the mountains are crushed and ground to powder, or torn from their roots.

6.explain: Habāʾan munbaththā: scattered dust, like the specks floating in a beam of sunlight. The earth is left flat, with no mountain or landmark.

7.explain: Azwājan thalāthah: three kinds, sorted by their good and bad deeds. The next three ayat name them.

8.explain: Aṣḥāb al-maymanah: those on the right, given their record in the right hand and taken to Paradise. The question “what are they?” shows how great their state is.

9.explain: Aṣḥāb al-mashʾamah: those on the left, given their record in the left hand and taken to the Fire. Here the same question shows how terrible their state is.

10.explain: As-sābiqūn as-sābiqūn: those foremost in good in this world are foremost into Paradise. They include the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs, and are fewer than those on the right.

11.explain: Al-muqarrabūn: the ones brought nearest to Allah, the highest rank.

12.explain: In jannāt an-naʿīm, gardens of delight, in the highest levels, with no rank above them.

13.explain: Thullah: a large crowd. Either from the earlier nations before the Prophet ﷺ, or from the early generations of this ummah.

14.explain: …and a few from the later people: from this ummah, or from its later generations. On the first view, the earlier nations had many prophets, so more early believers.

15.explain: Surur mawḍūnah: thrones woven with gold and jewels.

16.explain: Reclining at ease, mutaqābilīn: facing each other, no one looking at another’s back. It reflects their pure hearts and good manners.

17.explain: Wildān mukhalladūn: youths who serve them and never grow old or change.

18.explain: Akwāb are cups without handles, abārīq jugs with spouts, and kaʾs a glass filled from a flowing spring of wine that never runs dry.

19.explain: Unlike the wine of this world, it gives no headache (yuṣaddaʿūn) and does not take away the mind (yunzafūn).

20.explain: Any fruit they choose, whatever looks best to them and they crave.

21.explain: The meat of any bird they desire, prepared however they wish.

22.explain: Ḥūr ʿīn: companions with large, beautiful eyes, the white and the dark of the eye both striking.

23.explain: Like maknūn pearls: kept hidden, untouched, flawless in colour. So too these companions have no flaw at all.

24.explain: All this is jazāʾ, a reward for what they used to do. As their deeds were good, Allah made their reward good.

25.explain: They hear no laghw, empty or foul talk, and no taʾthīm, talk that brings sin.

26.explain: Only “Salām, salām”: they greet each other with peace. It is a home of good people, so only good speech is there.

27.explain: Now the second group, aṣḥāb al-yamīn, the righteous believers. They rank below the foremost, yet the question “what are they?” shows their state is still great.

28.explain: Sidr makhḍūd: lote trees with their thorns removed, or so laden with fruit the branches bend. Lote trees in this world are thorny, with little fruit.
28.why: Reportedly, Muslims admired the lote trees of Wajj, a fertile valley near Ṭāʾif, and wished they had the same. This ayah was then revealed.

29.explain: Ṭalḥ manḍūd: banana trees, their fruit layered from bottom to top. Or ṭalḥ is a large shade tree the Arabs knew.

30.explain: Ẓill mamdūd: shade that stretches on and never ends. A rider could travel a hundred years in the shade of one tree there.

31.explain: Māʾ maskūb: water poured out, flowing constantly over the ground.

32.explain: Fruit that is kathīrah: plentiful in amount and in kinds.

33.explain: Not maqṭūʿah, cut off when the season ends, and not mamnūʿah, kept from them by a price, a guard or distance.

34.explain: Furush marfūʿah: raised couches, high and soft. Or furush means wives, raised high in rank, which leads into the next ayat.

35.explain: Innā anshaʾnāhunna: We created them anew. Either the ḥūr, made without birth, or women of this world made young and beautiful. The Prophet ﷺ reportedly told an old woman she would enter Paradise young, and recited this.

37.explain: ʿUrub: loving and dear to their husbands. Atrāb: all of one age.

38.explain: Li-aṣḥāb al-yamīn: all this is prepared for those on the right.

39.explain: Thullah again: a large crowd from the earlier people. Either the nations before this ummah, or this ummah’s early generations.
39.why: Reportedly, ayah 14 (“a few of the later”) was hard on the Companions, and ʿUmar asked if only a few of them would be saved. Then 39–40 came, and the Prophet ﷺ hoped they would be half of Paradise.

40.explain: …and a large crowd from the later people. Unlike the foremost (13–14), this group is large from both.

41.explain: The third group, aṣḥāb ash-shimāl: those on the left, the people of the Fire. The question shows how dreadful their state is.

42.explain: Samūm: a scorching wind from the Fire that grips their breath. Ḥamīm: boiling water that tears their insides.

43.explain: Ẓill min yaḥmūm: a “shade” made of pitch-black smoke mixed with flame.

44.explain: Neither bārid, cool, nor karīm, pleasant to look at. It holds only distress and grief.

45.explain: Mutrafīn: in the world they lived in comfort and pleasure, which distracted them from obedience and from what the messengers brought.

46.explain: Yuṣirrūn ʿalā al-ḥinth al-ʿaẓīm: they kept on with the great sin and never repented. Mostly explained as shirk; also said to be their false oath that there is no resurrection.

47.explain: They mocked: “When we die and become dust and bones, will we really be raised?” They thought it impossible.

48.explain: “…and our forefathers too?” The ones long gone, they thought, could never come back.

49.explain: Say, O Prophet ﷺ: the earlier and the later generations, all of them…

50.explain: …will be gathered for the fixed time of a known Day. Not one will be left out, and it will come neither early nor late.

51.explain: Then you, aḍ-ḍāllūn al-mukadhdhibūn: astray from guidance and denying the Messenger ﷺ and what he brought.

52.explain: You will eat from the trees of zaqqūm, the ugliest and foulest-smelling of trees.

53.explain: Driven by a burning hunger, you will fill your bellies with it, yet it neither nourishes nor ends hunger.

54.explain: And on top of it you will drink ḥamīm, boiling water that seethes in the belly.

55.explain: You will drink like al-hīm: camels with a raging thirst, or with a disease that keeps them drinking and never satisfied.

56.explain: Hādhā nuzuluhum: this is their nuzul, the meal served to an arriving guest, on the Day of Recompense. For believers, the nuzul is Paradise.

57.explain: Naḥnu khalaqnākum: We created you from nothing. Fa-lawlā tuṣaddiqūn: so why not believe in the resurrection? The One able to begin creation can repeat it.

58.explain: Afa-raʾaytum: have you considered the fluid you emit into the womb?

59.explain: Do you create a person from it, or are We al-khāliqūn, the Creator? People play a tiny part; Allah shapes it stage by stage.

60.explain: Allah has decreed death for everyone, in heaven and on earth. Wa mā naḥnu bi-masbūqīn: no one outruns Him or defeats Him.

61.explain: …from replacing you with others like you, and remaking you in forms you do not know: changed on the Day of Resurrection, or as He changed some past peoples.

62.explain: An-nashʾah al-ūlā: you know the first creation, when you were nothing. Fa-lawlā tadhakkarūn: so why not remember He can create you again?

63.explain: Afa-raʾaytum mā taḥruthūn: have you considered the seed you plough into the earth?

64.explain: Do you make it grow, or are We az-zāriʿūn, the Grower? You only plough and plant. So the teaching: don’t say “I grew it”, say “I sowed it”.

65.explain: If He willed, He would turn it into ḥuṭām, dry stalks with no grain. Fa-ẓaltum tafakkahūn: you would be left stunned and regretful, or blaming one another.

66.explain: Saying: “Innā la-mughramūn: we have lost everything we spent on it.” Or: we are being punished.

67.explain: “No, we are maḥrūmūn, deprived of our harvest.” So thank Allah for crops that grow and survive.

68.explain: Afa-raʾaytum: have you considered the water you drink?

69.explain: Did you bring it down from al-muzn, the rain clouds, or are We the One who sends it down?

70.explain: If He willed, He would make it ujāj, too salty to drink or grow crops. Fa-lawlā tashkurūn: so why aren’t you grateful?

71.explain: Afa-raʾaytum: have you considered the fire you strike from green wood?

72.explain: Did you grow its tree, or are We al-munshiʾūn, the Producer? The Arabs rubbed green branches of two trees, markh and ʿafār, to make sparks.

73.explain: Allah made it a tadhkirah, a reminder of Hell’s far hotter fire, and matāʿ, a provision, for al-muqwīn: travellers in empty land, or everyone who uses it.

74.explain: Fa-sabbiḥ bismi rabbika al-ʿaẓīm: declare your Great Lord free of every flaw, the One who made water sweet and fire useful. Praise Him with heart, tongue and limbs.

75.explain: Fa-lā uqsimu: “No! I swear.” The lā rejects what they claim about the Quran. Mawāqiʿ an-nujūm: where the stars set, or the Quran’s parts revealed in stages.

76.explain: It is a mighty oath, if you only knew. The stars and their setting hold countless signs of His greatness.

77.explain: The point of the oath: innahu la-qurʾānun karīm, a noble Quran, full of good and knowledge. Not magic, poetry or the words of devils.

78.explain: Fī kitābin maknūn: in a guarded Book, the Preserved Tablet, hidden from creation and beyond the devils’ reach.

79.explain: Lā yamassuhu illā al-muṭahharūn: only the purified touch it, meaning the angels. Many also take it to mean the muṣḥaf is touched only in purity, as a letter of the Prophet ﷺ said.

80.explain: Tanzīl: sent down from the Lord of the worlds, not magic or poetry as they claim.

81.explain: Mudhinūn: do you take this speech lightly, deny it, or hide it for fear of people? The word comes from rubbing on oil: going soft where you should stand firm.

82.explain: You make your thanks for provision, or your share of the Quran, nothing but denial: as when rain falls and people credit a star, not Allah.
82.why: Reportedly, after rain fell, some people said “such-and-such star was right”, and 75–82 were revealed. In another report, a man said “we were watered by such a star” after the Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain.

83.explain: Fa-lawlā: then why not, when the soul of a dying person reaches al-ḥulqūm, the throat…

84.explain: …while you, his family, stand watching him, unable to do anything.

85.explain: We are nearer to him than you, by Our knowledge and Our angels, but you cannot see.

86.explain: If you really are ghayra madīnīn, never to be raised and repaid, as you claim…

87.explain: …then bring the soul back to its body, if you are truthful. You cannot, so the matter belongs to Allah.

88.explain: Fa-ammā in kāna: if the dying person is of al-muqarrabūn, the brought-near: those who did the duties and the extras, and left the forbidden and the disliked.

89.explain: Rawḥ: rest, joy and mercy. Rayḥān: provision, or sweet fragrance. And a garden of delight. This good news reaches them at death.

90.explain: Wa-ammā in kāna: and if he is of aṣḥāb al-yamīn, who did the duties and left the forbidden, even with some shortcomings…

91.explain: Salāmun laka: “Peace to you, you are of the people of the right.” The angels greet him, or his brothers on the right do; he is safe from punishment.

92.explain: Wa-ammā in kāna: but if he is of al-mukadhdhibīn aḍ-ḍāllīn, who denied the truth and strayed from guidance…

93.explain: …then his nuzul, the welcome served to a guest, is ḥamīm, boiling water.

94.explain: …and taṣliyat jaḥīm: burning in the blazing Fire, which surrounds him from every side.

95.explain: Ḥaqq al-yaqīn: all of this, the reward and the punishment, is the certain truth, with no doubt and no escape.

96.explain: The same words as ayah 74. When fa-sabbiḥ bismi rabbika al-ʿaẓīm came, the Prophet ﷺ reportedly said, “Put it in your rukūʿ,” where he would say subḥāna rabbiya al-ʿaẓīm.
